title: Too Heavy to Swim
connection_reasons: The lyric is about being too tired to keep swimming, and you named this quiet, minor-key loop 'lake bottoms'. Both are about sinking under a weight.

fragments.suggestion: The image of a skill being lost, holding your breath for a whole song, carries more weight than drowning would. 'The water's not cold it's just heavy' refuses the obvious reading, which keeps it honest. It reads as a turn in a larger piece, a moment where the mood drops lower before anything resolves. Sing it close and low.

fragments.title: lake bottoms
fragments.suggestion: A quiet 28-second loop at 136 BPM in A minor, mid-range in tone and moderately busy. The low level and minor key give it a heavy, submerged feel even at this tempo. Reversing a section and layering it under the forward version would deepen that underwater quality. Its mood is the same from start to end; consider breaking it once, with a single brighter chord or a filter opening, before it returns to depth. Keep anything added above it soft so the weight of the loop stays in front.
